title: Bracket IPv6 literals when formatting upstream CONNECT authority
answers: Why does an upstream proxy reject CONNECT requests with malformed authority when targeting IPv6?
How to format IPv6 addresses in mitmproxy upstream proxy CONNECT requests and Host headers?
Why does --mode upstream fail to establish connection to an IPv6 target server?
body:
Symptom: Upstream proxies reject HTTP CONNECT requests with malformed authority errors when mitmproxy runs in upstream mode (--mode upstream) with an IPv6 target.
Root cause: mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/_upstream_proxy.py:start_handshake concatenated raw IPv6 addresses directly as host:port without RFC 3986 square brackets.
Fix pattern: Check if ipaddress.ip_address(host) is an IPv6Address and wrap the literal in square brackets (b"[" + host.encode() + b"]") before appending the port.
Constraints: Applies when formatting HTTP authorities or Host headers for IPv6 target literals; domain names (IDNA-encoded) and IPv4 addresses must remain unbracketed.
applies: mitmproxy upstream mode HTTP CONNECT authority and Host header generation
says: Upstream proxy rejects connection requests when forwarding traffic to an IPv6 server.
Connecting through a parent proxy fails when the target destination is an IPv6 address.
Targeting IPv6 addresses in upstream proxy mode triggers invalid request destination errors.
Allow forwarding secure connections through upstream proxies when target hosts are IPv6 literals.
